points.reason: The bus write directly changes ctrl.enable, including writing zero to disable the engine.
The inverted enable drives the FIFO clear control, so disabling the setting can discard queued transfers.
The another-IP FIFO receives tx_fifo.clear and can clear the queued transmit data.
This block uses enable only to qualify the interrupt request and does not store, clear, or gate the NeoLED engine itself.
ctrl.enable is loaded into serial.state(2), and the state machine uses that state to enter or leave engine operation.
The output directly reflects ctrl.enable, so changing the setting changes the clock-generator request and can disable operation.
A bus write directly replaces the stored serial mode setting.
This signal only forwards the mode bit as part of a queued transmit word.
The FIFO buffers the queued word; the RTL shows no independent mode check or mode modification at this point.
The FIFO word's mode bit selects the serial mode and payload length, changing the generated frame.
The selected serial mode chooses which shift-register bit becomes the next transmitted bit.
A bus write directly replaces the stored strobe setting.
This signal only forwards the strobe bit as part of a queued transmit word.
The FIFO buffers the queued word and the RTL shows no independent strobe decision inside this unit at this point.
The queued strobe bit selects the serial engine state path through the condition on tx_fifo.rdata(33).
The selected state controls when the queued strobe-bearing word is removed for transmission.
A bus write changes the stored clock-source selector, including selecting a source that does not provide useful pacing.
ctrl.clk_prsc indexes clkgen_i to make serial.pulse_clk, and the engine advances only when that pulse is asserted.
Bus writes directly replace the total-period and zero/one high-time settings.
The settings select t_high and determine pulse and strobe counter progression used to generate the waveform.
The selected data bit decides whether t0_high or t1_high is loaded for the next waveform interval.
The bus data is placed into the FIFO write word, so changing the input changes the queued payload.
The address, direction, and strobe jointly decide whether a payload word is written, allowing a transfer to be omitted or gated.
By the another-IP black-box rule, the FIFO stores the write word and returns it on rdata, while its write and read controls can prevent the payload from reaching the engine.
